question.text: When there is a change in the fundamental attributes of a mutual fund scheme, the AMC is required to:

answer.text: Give written notice to unitholders and provide them an exit option at NAV without any exit load
Obtain prior approval from SEBI before implementing any changes
Automatically convert existing units to the new scheme structure without notice
Publish a notice only in newspapers and no direct communication to unitholders is needed

explanation.text: The Logic: When fundamental attributes of a scheme change (such as investment objective, asset allocation pattern, or scheme type), the AMC must send a written communication to each unitholder and issue an advertisement, and must provide a 30-day exit option at the prevailing NAV without any exit load. In addition, the trustees shall take the comments of the Board (SEBI) before bringing such change. This combination of written communication, advertisement, exit window, and Board comments protects investors who may not agree with the new attributes. The Trap: The change cannot be implemented silently or only through a newspaper notice; written communication to unitholders is mandatory. Existing units are not converted automatically, and unitholders cannot be denied the load-free 30-day exit option. Note: Anchor your answer to the four source-backed elements: written communication, advertisement, 30-day exit at prevailing NAV without exit load, and trustees taking Board comments before bringing the change.
